catalog_citation: van der Wilden, Jaap and Jelly van der Wilden. 1975. Kemtuk Phonology. Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya Development IV(3): 31-60. Abepura: Institute for Anthropology, Cenderawasih University. (papuaweb.org scan, Internet Archive copy 20030421)
catalog_quote: The phonological word (PW) functions within the higher phonological phrase and provides a useful construction for specifying underlying stress and syllable patterns. 1.1 Stress Patterns. PWs are constructed of one to three syllables². They are of two general contrastive classes: ultimate stress and penultimate stress³. 1.11 Ultimate Stress. All possible ultimate stress PWs may be derived from the following schematic string (where S = syllable and ´ = stress): (S) S) Ś. Monosyllabic and disyllabic PWs are derived from this formula. Note the following examples: /bu/ [bu] 'water/air' ... /mi.á/ [mi̯á] 'mother/ibu', /naŋ.glík/ [nʌŋglík] 'three/tiga'. Following are examples of three syllable ultimate stress forms (the ante-penultimate syllable receiving a phonetically slightly stronger stress than the penultimate, but still not so strong as the ultimate stress): /bA.kA.nán/ [bakʌnʌ́ŋ] 'bran…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The record rests on the primary and only phonology of Kemtuik (van der Wilden & van der Wilden 1975, Irian IV(3):31-60), which we hold as a papuaweb/the Internet Archive page-image scan; the deciding quotation (two contrastive stress classes, ultimate ((S)S)Ś vs penultimate (S)ŚS, with examples and notes 2, 3, 6, 7) is confirmed verbatim on pp. 32-33, 59-60. The lexical coding with a right-edge two-syllable window follows directly from the source's own statement and example lists (e.g. /mi.á/ vs /bÁ.nu/). No later phonology, grammar, dissertation or instrumental study exists per Glottolog, OLAC, Crossref and WALS; the only unheld descriptive works are the same authors' 1991 sketch+dictionary and 2012 dictionary, which might refine counts or per-word marking but are unlikely to overturn the classification.
